maria: Quick follow-up from the region-handshake RFC — observed a staging incident where EU-resident tenant writes were accepted in us-west during a partial partition. How do we want to enforce data residency for active-active? :thinking:

derek: Current flow is residency-routing + lease check. But leases can be stale under partition so a node in us-west may accept and replicate later — which violates residency constraints. We discussed stricter modes in the RFC but didn't land on an implementation.

sam: Proposal sketch: per-tenant `residency.mode = [soft|strict|quarantine]`.
- soft: current behavior (local accept + async replicate)
- strict: proxy to resident region synchronously (or reject after timeout)
- quarantine: accept locally, mark write as quarantined until resident ack (not visible to user)

eva: Strict mode guarantees compliance but p99 latency will jump on cross-region proxy. Quarantine keeps latency but complicates client semantics and could surprise product teams.

jon: Quarantine also creates audit surface — we need strong metadata + automatic rollback if resident never acks. Also billing implications if we delay commits.

maria: Let's call out tradeoffs explicitly:
1) Strong sync proxy: correctness, high latency, dependent on inter-region connectivity.
2) Local accept + quarantine: low latency, eventual compliance, complex visible state transitions.
3) Fail-open read-only: non-resident regions become read-only for that tenant until resident resumes — avoids wrong writes but may degrade UX.

sam: Example config I was thinking (console + API):
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acct_123",
  "residency": {
    "regions": ["eu-west-1"],
    "mode": "strict",
    "proxy_timeout_ms": 500
  }
}
```

eva: For rollout, default to `soft` for historical tenants. New customers can opt into `strict` via onboarding. We'll need perf benchmarks for strict mode (p50/p99) and a feature flag to enable in Dedicated/Private.

derek: Instrumentation needed: `residency.proxy.latency`, `residency.quarantine.count`, `residency.rejects`, `residency.handoff.errors`. Add alerts when proxy latencies exceed SLO or quarantine backlog grows.

infra-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pulls/2345 — "residency: add strict/quarantine modes" :rocket:

maria: Next concrete steps: 1) Draft short RFC add modes + state machine for quarantined writes (owner: @derek). 2) Telemetry + alerting spec (owner: @derek). 3) Runbook/playbook for operators + client SDK guidance on retry semantics (owners: @eva for runbook, @sam for SDK). 4) Canary flow + perf harness to validate p99 impact (owner: @eva).

derek: I'll draft the RFC and mock the state transitions (Accepted -> Quarantined -> ResidentAcked | ResidentRejected | QuarantineTimeout -> Rollback).

sam: I'll add SDK retry/backoff examples and console toggle UX. Also will add a diagnostic header `X-Residency-Status` so customers can detect quarantined state.

eva: I'll own the runbook and perf harness; will add a page to ops runbooks with play actions: `promote-resident-lease`, `drain-quarantine`, `force-rollback`.

maria: Great. Let's sync on a short doc tomorrow. If anyone disagrees with owners ping here. :eyes: 

derek: ack — will post RFC link once draft is ready.

sam: ack.

eva: ack.

maria: Closing the thread once RFC is up; thanks all.
